meta.title: Is Directive 8020 Multiplayer, Split Screen or Crossplay? (Co-Op Guide)
meta.description: Directive 8020 has local Movie Night co-op for up to 5 players. No split screen, no online mode, no crossplay yet. Full co-op Q&A.

hero.h1: Is Directive 8020 Multiplayer, Split Screen or Crossplay?
hero.tagline: Local Movie Night co-op only — no split screen, no online mode yet.
hero.intro: Everything you need to know about Directive 8020's co-op modes, answered question by question.

blocks.text: Yes, but only locally at launch. **Movie Night** mode supports up to **5 players** passing a single controller on one screen. There is no online multiplayer yet.

**No — there is no split screen in Directive 8020.** Movie Night is a **single-screen, hot-seat mode**: everyone watches the same screen, and the controller is passed to whoever's character is in the scene. The game prompts you with the player's name when it's their turn. Think party game pass-the-controller, not two halves of a TV.

Confused by the Steam page? Steam lists **“Shared/Split Screen Co-op”** as one combined tag — a game earns it through either half. Directive 8020 qualifies through the **“Shared Screen”** half: the whole couch watches one screen together. The picture is never split.

**Not yet — but it is confirmed to be coming.** Supermassive Games announced online Movie Night as a free post-launch update that mirrors the couch co-op experience with up to 5 players, and their [June 2026 patch notes](https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2255370/view/673997481174894605) reconfirm it: “Regarding online multiplayer, it's definitely coming and the team is hard at work.” No release date has been announced yet.

**No.** There is no crossplay in Directive 8020 — the online mode is not out yet, so there is nothing to crossplay across. No crossplay announcement has been made for the upcoming online Movie Night update either.

sections.heading: How does local co-op (Movie Night) work?

blocks.text: Start a new game, choose **Movie Night**, and assign each of the 5 playable characters to a player. When a player's character is in a scene, the controller is handed to them. Players can **vote on key decisions** together, and the group can use Turning Points to rewind deaths and retry sections.

items: Assign characters based on how much screen time they get — Osmond has the most, Cooper has less
Use the **Shared Controller** option if you don't have enough controllers
Agree on decision rules beforehand — votes on major choices are where Movie Night nights are won or lost

sections.heading: How do you invite friends to play?

blocks.text: Locally, friends join by sitting on the couch — there is nothing to invite them to until the **online Movie Night update** arrives. When it ships, invites will work through your platform's friend list.

**Not on Steam** — Remote Play Together is not a listed feature for Directive 8020. The Steam page lists **Remote Play on TV**, which is different: that streams from your PC to a screen in your own home, not to friends.

**PlayStation Share Play** and **Xbox screen sharing** do work as workarounds today, since they work with any game — the host runs Movie Night and remote friends take turns through the stream. Just expect some input lag and video compression.
The online 2-player **Shared Story** mode from earlier Dark Pictures games is **not included in Directive 8020**. The studio consolidated co-op into Movie Night only.

sections.heading: Does Directive 8020 have a friend pass?

blocks.text: **No friend pass has been announced.** For local Movie Night you only need **one copy of the game** — everyone plays on the same screen. For the upcoming online Movie Night update, plan on each player owning their own copy.

sections.heading: How many players can play Directive 8020?

blocks.text: **Up to 5 players** in Movie Night mode. You can also play with **2, 3, or 4 players** — just split the 5 playable characters between the players present.
